final_candidates.decision_summary: High escape (z=0.847) combined with the strongest plm plausibility (0.056) and best MSA mutant frequency (~13.5%) among leaders, supporting retained replication fitness.
Highest escape score (z=0.895) with the top plm plausibility (0.058); low MSA mutant frequency is the only concern, hence rank 2.
Second-highest escape (z=0.855) but near-zero plm and low MSA frequency raise replication-fitness risk; retained at reduced confidence as the best remaining escape option.

stop_reason.detail: Evidence is saturated across available applicable tools and the Top-3 ranking has converged; structure evidence is unavailable for this task.

history.rationale: Removes the N330 (HXB2 N332) glycan supersite, a well-characterized escape route from PGT128-class bNAbs; BG505 retains fitness without this glycan.
PNGS loss at Asn330 in the V3/C3 glycan shield region is a classic escape mechanism; awaiting EVEscape and ESM-1v confirmation.
Decent escape (0.737) but very low plausibility (0.001) implies likely fitness defect; demoted.
Moderate escape but zero plm and zero MSA frequency at a conserved position (entropy 1.838); fitness risk too high.

rejection.reason: Moderate escape but zero plm and zero MSA frequency at a conserved position (entropy 1.838); fitness risk too high.

history.rationale: Eliminates the N301 N-linked glycan at the V3 base (NNT motif), known to modulate V3-directed and glycan-dependent antibody recognition with modest fitness cost.
V3-base glycan loss typically confers broad antibody escape with modest fitness cost.
Weakest escape among viable-scoring candidates (0.618) plus very low plausibility; demoted.
Lowest escape among retainable candidates with zero plm and zero MSA frequency; rejected.

rejection.reason: Lowest escape among retainable candidates with zero plm and zero MSA frequency; rejected.

history.rationale: Removes the V1-loop N136 (NIT) glycan, altering shielding of the V1/V2 apex targeted by PG9/PG16-class antibodies; glutamine keeps side-chain size similar.
V1 glycan repositioning/loss candidate; conservative Asn-to-Gln change should preserve folding.
Good escape (0.787) but near-zero plausibility (0.004), suggesting fitness cost; demoted.
Solid escape (0.787) with best MSA coverage (app 0.99) and modest mutant frequency; best backup, moves to rank 4.
Disrupts the C2-region N288 (NTP) glycan site that contributes to surface shielding; glycan repositioning is a common escape mechanism with limited structural disruption.
C2-region glycan candidate; conservative substitution limits fitness risk.
Moderate escape (0.693) with reasonable plausibility (0.033); kept mid-pool.
Moderate escape (0.693) with the second-best MSA/plm profile; retains rank 5 as alternate.
Removes the V4-region N459 (NST) glycan, reducing the dense V4 glycan shield exploited for escape; serine is a conservative substitution at an exposed loop.
C4/V5-region glycan loss candidate potentially affecting bNAb access.
Second-best combination: strong escape (0.847) and second-highest plausibility (0.056); promoted to rank 2.
High escape (0.847), best plm plausibility among leaders (0.056), and by far the strongest MSA support (13.5% mutant frequency, app 0.82) — promotes to rank 1.
Abolishes the N361 (NSS) glycan near the V3/C3 boundary, potentially shifting the local glycan fence; aspartate preserves negative polarity at a surface site.
Introduces negative charge in CD4bs-adjacent region; may disrupt some bNAb epitopes but carries higher fitness risk.
Solid escape (0.786) with moderate plausibility (0.028); retained as a strong backup just outside Top-3.
Good escape (0.786) but zero observed D frequency in 75 homologs weakens the replication-fitness case; demoted below N136Q/N288Q.
Charge reversal at the V3-loop base (K304) can disrupt binding of V3-targeting antibodies while the flexible loop tolerates substitutions without folding cost.
Charge reversal in V3 tip-adjacent region could perturb antibody binding but risks fitness.
Very high escape (0.855) but low sequence plausibility (0.008), raising replication-fitness concerns; ranked 3rd as a higher-risk escape option.
Second-highest escape (0.855) but near-zero plm (0.008) and low MSA frequency (0.013) raise replication-fitness concerns; holds rank 3 with reduced confidence.
Removes the C1-proximal N87 (NVT) glycan that contributes to trimer shielding; conservative Asn->Gln limits structural perturbation.
C1 glycan; conservative change, but C1 mutations can impair trimer assembly.
Lowest escape score (0.516) and essentially zero plausibility; rejected.

rejection.reason: Lowest escape score (0.516) and essentially zero plausibility; rejected.

history.rationale: Substitution at the V3 crown GPGQ arch can distort the tip conformation recognized by V3 bNAbs, but carries some risk to Env function given the conserved crown.
V3 crown substitution could strongly affect neutralization but risks disrupting V3 conformation.
Middling escape (0.645) with essentially zero plausibility; rejected.

rejection.reason: Middling escape (0.645) with essentially zero plausibility; rejected.

history.rationale: Removes the V4-adjacent N396 (NTS) glycan, thinning local shielding against glycan-dependent antibodies; solvent-exposed loop site likely tolerates the change.
CD4bs-loop glycan candidate; charge introduction adds escape potential with moderate fitness risk.
Highest EVEscape score (0.895) combined with the highest ESM-1v plausibility (0.058) in the pool — best escape-with-fitness trade-off; moves to rank 1.
Highest escape (0.895) and best plm (0.058), but MSA mutant frequency is only 0.016; moves to rank 2.
